_about: Per-model context windows and degradation bands used by ctxhealth.py. Bands are research-derived ESTIMATES of a gradual gradient, not cliffs (Chroma Context Rot 2025; Anthropic 'gradient not cliff' guidance). Evidence and search plan: RESEARCH.md. Edit families/match to add a model; never hand-edit thresholds without logging a C- entry in CHANGELOG.md.

profiles._about: Fractions of the model's NATIVE window at which each band starts: [watch, caution, warning, critical]. Keyed by model class. 'balanced' is the default; 'conservative' reproduces the original 2026-08-29 absolute bands for 1M models (100K/200K/400K/600K); 'relaxed' follows the later evidence (Verdent: onset ~400K, unreliable past ~600K on Sonnet 4.6; Opus 4.6 MRCR 93% at 256K -> 76% at 1M).

green.label: GREEN
green.effects: no measurable effect for most tasks

watch.label: WATCH
watch.effects: mild; recall of mid-session details starts to soften
watch.advice: fine to continue; start the next big task in a fresh session

caution.label: CAUTION
caution.effects: noticeable; weaker mid-session recall, instruction drift, more lost-in-the-middle misses
caution.advice: finish the current piece of work here, then start a new session; offer a handoff summary (decisions, open items, file paths)

warning.label: WARNING
warning.effects: significant; retrieval of specific earlier facts is unreliable
warning.advice: start a new session now unless mid-critical-step; write a handoff summary file first

critical.label: CRITICAL
critical.effects: severe; retrieval unreliable and auto-compaction is near, which silently summarizes history
critical.advice: write the handoff summary now, then start a new session

unknown_model.label: unrecognized model (assumed 200K)
unknown_model.note: Add the id to a family in models.json; the refresh procedure in MAINTENANCE.md covers new models.

families.label: Claude 1M-class
families.note: Fable 5.1 / Mythos 5.1 / Opus 5.5 / Opus 5 / Sonnet 5 / Opus 4.6-4.8 / Sonnet 4.6: 1M input, 128K output (300K output on the Batch API with a beta header). Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5, released 2026-09-22) matches claude-opus-5*; 1M on every Claude Code plan (Opus 4.7 and later) and the `opus` alias and `default` model since Claude Code v2.1.280. Its thinking is always on and it thinks more per turn than Opus 5 at the same effort (most at xhigh/max), so on long tool loops context grows faster per turn; the Claude Code default effort is medium. No independent long-context benchmark published for the 5.x models yet (the Opus 5.5 system card gives only ProgramBench, an agentic benchmark with episodes up to 1M: 91.2% vs Opus 5 85.4%, not split by length); bands come from Opus 4.6 MRCR (93% at 256K, 76% at 1M) and Sonnet 4.6 field reports (onset ~400K, unreliable past ~600K). Claude Code: auto-compact at roughly window minus ~33K (Sonnet 5 documented ~967K); CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT=1 caps at 200K.

families.label: Claude 200K-class
families.note: Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 4.5, Opus 4.5 and older: 200K. The trailing claude-* pattern catches unknown Claude ids conservatively; newer Claude models are 1M, so add them to claude-1m when they appear.

families.label: GPT-6 Sol / Luna (922K input)
families.note: Released 2026-09-22: 1,050,000 total, 922K input, 128K output; the window here is the 922K input limit, since the meter counts input and a 1.05M base put the relaxed critical band (945K) past what the model accepts (secondary sources; openai.com returns 403 to fetch). Sol $2/$10, Luna $0.10/$0.50 per MTok, input past 272K billed at 2x. Trained with methods like GPT-6 Astra's, but no MRCR or other long-context score is published for either, so Astra's 96.3% does not carry over and the bands are the 1M-class defaults. In Codex from 0.156.x (model picker) and listed in GitHub Copilot; no Codex window cap is documented for them, so the Codex parser relies on token_count model_context_window.

families.label: GPT-6 Astra (1M)
families.note: Released 2026-09-03/04; 1M-token window (OpenAI). MRCR v2 8-needle: 100% at 256K-512K, 96.3% at 512K-1M, the strongest long-context score published so far. Default model in Codex CLI since v0.153.1; Codex users configure a 600K window for it (openai/codex#45074: effective 95%, auto-compact 90%, and the internal count can exceed the displayed one by 200K+, so treat Codex numbers on Astra as rough). Secondary sources give 922K input / 128K output and recommend auto_compact_token_limit 850000. The gpt-6* pattern also catches GPT-6 ids not listed above (Sol and Luna have their own family) until they are verified.

families.label: GPT-5.6 Sol / Terra / Luna (272K)
families.note: Codex changelog corrected the GPT-5.6 windows to 272,000 (via secondary report); Cursor lists GPT-5.6 at 272K. MRCR v2 8-needle: Sol 91.5% at 256K-512K, 73.8% at 512K-1M (OpenAI, quoted against Astra). Verify against a primary OpenAI page on the next refresh. llm-stats (self-reported, 2026-09-23) also lists Terra 0.896 and Luna 0.413, so Luna is far weaker at long context than Sol or Terra.

families.label: GPT-5.5 (1M native)
families.note: OpenAI: ~1.05M window. MRCR v2 8-needle: 90% at 32-64K, 83% at 64-128K, 74% at 512K-1M. Codex CLI caps it at 400K (harness entry) and field reports show the effective budget oscillating 258K-353K (openai/codex#30875).

families.label: GPT-5.4 (256K)
families.note: 256K window; MRCR 8-needle 36.6% at 1M-scale tests means it was already weak beyond its window's midpoint. mini/nano variants (2026-03) unverified; treated the same.

families.label: GPT-5.x / Codex 400K-class
families.note: GPT-5 / 5.1 / 5.2 / 5.3-Codex families: 400K window (Copilot's /models endpoint lists context_window 400000 with max_prompt 128K-272K). Also the catch-all for later gpt-5.x ids until verified.

families.label: OpenAI legacy (128-200K)
families.note: o-series 200K, gpt-4o 128K; retired from ChatGPT in early 2026, may still appear in API/Copilot ids.

families.label: Gemini (1M)
families.note: Gemini 3 / 3.1 Pro and the 3.x Flash line (3.8 Flash released 2026-09-02): 1,048,576 input, 65,536 output. Long-context quality now differs sharply within the family: MRCR v2 8-needle (llm-stats, self-reported) Gemini 3.7 Flash 97%, 3.6 Flash 54%, 3.1 Pro 26% at 1M (77% at 128K for 3 Pro), so the 1M window is far more usable on 3.7+ Flash than on Pro. Gemini CLI compresses history automatically at model.compressionThreshold (default 0.5, confirmed 2026-09 in the config reference; contextManagement.historyWindow maxTokens 150000 / retainedTokens 40000).

families.label: Grok 4.5 (500K)
families.note: Added to Copilot 2026-07-28 with up to 500K context.

harnesses._about: Caps the host tool imposes on top of the model's native window, and where it auto-compacts. by_family keys are family ids above. A window reported by the harness itself (Claude Code statusline context_window_size, Codex model_context_window, Cursor preCompact context_window_size) always wins; then ~/.ctxhealth/config.json windows.<harness>; then these defaults; then native. VS Code agent sessions are measured by their transcript: a Copilot events.jsonl gets the copilot cap, a Codex rollout the codex cap, a Claude transcript the native window.

claude.label: Claude Code
claude.note: Native window by default for 1M models (Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, Opus 5, Sonnet 5, Opus 4.6+; 4.7+ on every plan without [1m]). Auto-compacts at about window minus 33K (Sonnet 5: ~967K); /autocompact, --autocompact, CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW override. Hooks: UserPromptSubmit + SessionStart inject context; statusLine gives exact usage. code.claude.com/docs/en/context-window (2026-09-15) gives the startup breakdown (system prompt ~4.2K, MCP tools deferred by default, skills index not re-injected after /compact); changelog 2.1.273 (2026-09-15) fixed a context meter that double-counted advisor-tool turns and made auto-compact fire near half the real window, which explains earlier observed 83-90% compactions on 200K windows. 2.1.274 makes hook-driven sessions compact instead of ending with 'Prompt is too long'; 2.1.280 (2026-09-22) makes Opus 5.5 the default model on Pro through Enterprise (1M either way).

cowork.label: Cowork (Claude Desktop)
cowork.note: Runs no hooks (claude-code#63360, #47993); the skill is the only in-session layer. A fresh session starts near 105K because of the loaded tool and skill catalog, so growth above that floor is the signal.

copilot.label: Copilot CLI
copilot.note: 200K default cap (128K usable prompt on older models per /models endpoint), 1M opt-in since 2026-06-04 in VS Code and Copilot CLI: `config set windows.copilot 1000000`. Auto-compacts at ~80%. /context and /usage (and VS Code's chat-input meter) are authoritative. events.jsonl usage records are not a stable API (copilot-cli#3551); the parser falls back to a size estimate. Fable 5.1 and Gemini 3.8 Flash added 2026-09 (admin-enabled); CLI v1.0.81 hook inputs carry traceparent/tracestate and JSON output files carry per-agent usage (unverified live). Opus 5.5 added 2026-09-22 (Pro+, Max, Business, Enterprise; gradual rollout; context cap not stated, assume the 200K default). Copilot CLI support for claude-opus-5.5 from v1.0.89-0 (prerelease).

codex.label: Codex CLI
codex.note: token_count events carry model_context_window (authoritative) and last_token_usage. model_auto_compact_token_limit defaults vary by model (<= 90% of the window). /status shows the percentage since v0.121. GPT-6 Astra (default since v0.153.1): users configure 600K; openai/codex#45074 shows compaction firing at an internal 623K while the UI showed ~388K, so on Astra report the number as rough and flag compaction proximity from model_context_window, not the displayed count. Docs moved to learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks; hooks gained async and mcp_tool types, additionalContextLimit 2,500 tokens. PR #45094 (merged 2026-09-12) estimates history tokens from content instead of serialized envelopes, which may narrow the #45074 gap (issue still open 2026-09-22); compaction on GPT-6 models is reported slow (#45433, 2-3+ minutes; #43062, hangs of 20+ minutes). GPT-6 Sol (openai/codex#47805, 0.156.1, 2026-09-24): Codex's catalog has context_window 272,000 (effective 95%, about 258.4K) and max_context_window 872,000; a model_context_window override of 1M is cut to 828.4K; Luna presumably the same. 0.157.0 resumes from the latest compaction boundary, so read the last token_count, never a sum.

gemini.label: Gemini CLI
gemini.note: Footer shows '(NN% context left)' natively; saved chats carry no token counts, so this tool only estimates from file size. Compression at model.compressionThreshold (0.5 documented) is routine, not a warning.

cursor.label: Cursor
cursor.note: Default caps: Sonnet 5 200K, Opus 5 / Fable 5.1 300K, GPT-5.6 272K, Gemini 200K; Max mode 1M (`config set windows.cursor 1000000`). The chat context ring is authoritative; preCompact hooks receive exact context_tokens. Opus 5.5 (matched to claude-1m): Cursor's model page says up to 1M with no long-context surcharge but gives no default (non-Max) cap; 300K assumed as for Opus 5 / Fable 5.1. The models, max-mode and pricing pages no longer carry a cap table.

baseline._about: Startup (initial) context: the input of the session's FIRST assistant turn minus the estimated first prompt, i.e. system prompt + tool/MCP schemas + project instruction files + memory + skills catalog. Bands are fractions of the EFFECTIVE (harness) window, [notable, high, excessive], keyed by model class. They are JUDGMENT ESTIMATES seeded 2026-09-05 from the degradation evidence (instruction adherence softening near 20% of a 1M window; lost-in-the-middle pushing prefix instructions mid-window as the session grows; 200K-class harnesses compacting at 80-90%) and from observed platform floors (Cowork ~105K). RESEARCH.md 'Startup context' tracks the evidence; refine per model and platform there, log a C- entry when these move. Live measurements live in ~/.ctxhealth/baseline/<platform>.jsonl.

notable.label: NOTABLE
notable.effects: sizable startup block; the instructions in it sit mid-window sooner as the session grows, and working room is reduced
notable.advice: no action needed now; when the inventory runs, look for a block that is not earning its keep (unused MCP servers, imported docs, skills catalog)

high.label: HIGH
high.effects: a fifth or more of the window is spent before the first prompt; on 200K-class models this cuts working room sharply and pushes prefix instructions into the lost-in-the-middle zone early
high.advice: trim the startup context for this platform: disconnect unused MCP servers, split or shorten instruction-file imports, or use a bigger-window model here

excessive.label: EXCESSIVE
excessive.effects: most of the usable window is startup material; expect weaker instruction following from the first turn and early compaction
excessive.advice: reduce the startup context before continuing; this model/platform combination starts already degraded

typical._about: Observed startup sizes for orientation only; ~/.ctxhealth/baseline is the live record.

selection._about: Selection noise: how many SKILLS/tools compete for the model's choice at startup, which is a separate failure mode from size. A catalog can be cheap in tokens (name+description only) and still cost accuracy, because the model picks by matching the prompt against every description. Evidence (2026-09-06): chance-corrected tool-retrieval work (arXiv 2605.24660) finds standard retrievers degrade well before the catalog is large and that semantically near-duplicate entries ('calc_area_triangle' vs 'calculate_triangle_area') are the dominant difficulty, not raw count; survey numbers put ~50 tools at 84-95% selection accuracy, ~200 tools at 41-83%, ~740 tools at 0-20%; practitioner reports put the onset of overlap confusion around 30 entries and Anthropic's skills playbook draws its line at 8-12 skills. Claude Code itself caps the listing with skillListingBudgetFraction (default 0.01 of the window) and skillListingMaxDescChars (default 1536), dropping WHOLE descriptions for least-invoked skills when over budget - so an oversized catalog silently makes rare skills invisible rather than truncating evenly. Bands below are entry COUNTS of the visible catalog. Refine in RESEARCH.md 'Selection noise'; log a C- entry when they move.

notable.label: NOTABLE
notable.effects: the catalog is past the point where descriptions start to overlap; occasional wrong-skill or missed-skill picks
notable.advice: scope the project-specific skills to their own repo's .claude/skills instead of the user-level root

high.label: HIGH
high.effects: selection accuracy measurably drops in this range and near-duplicate entries compete; Claude Code's listing budget may already be dropping least-invoked descriptions, making them uninvokable
high.advice: cut the catalog to the skills this project can actually use: park the out-of-scope ones outside every skills root and link them per-repo

excessive.label: EXCESSIVE
excessive.effects: catalogs this size land in the band where reported selection accuracy falls off sharply, and rare skills are effectively invisible under the listing budget
excessive.advice: park most of the catalog now; keep a small always-on set and link the rest per-repo

selection.listing_note: code.claude.com/docs/en/skills (2026-09): the skills listing budget scales at 1% of the model's context window; descriptions are shortened to fit and, on overflow, dropped starting with the least-invoked skills; description plus when_to_use truncates at 1,536 characters; disable-model-invocation skills are excluded; the listing is not re-injected after /compact. The setting keys skillListingBudgetFraction / skillListingMaxDescChars appear only in third-party guides, not on the settings reference.
